PLE: Physical-Engineering’s Last Exam

paper.arxiv.2610.30537

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at 2610.30537v2. Constraint-gated objective grading and separate engineering-task routes establish evaluation protocol scope. Planned public29and85total tasks do not establish observed release availability or code/physics validity. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The hybrid score is s = 0.4 p + 0.6 G Oprime: a failed hard-constraint gate removes objective credit but does not generally zero the constraint-fraction term. Single-task run variance and model-judge self-preference are reported; benchmark scores therefore cannot certify safety, feasibility or real engineering deployment readiness.

Permanent record ID: repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2610.30537.limitation

  • This is a source-specific, first-party description; this repair does not independently reproduce experiments or audit operational execution and customer outcomes.
  • Forty-four tasks are authored end to end by Mercor-recruited practising engineers. Forty-one coauthored tasks use engineer briefs, Claude Opus 5 Creator/Claude Code and Solver/Hermes, followed by expert validation and difficulty intensification.
  • Expert tasks use weighted binary rubrics judged by Claude Opus 5.5. Thirty-seven coauthored tasks use constraint/objective scoring, while four site/MEP tasks retain bespoke graders; selected narrative items are also model-judged.
  • The hybrid score is s=0.4p+0.6G Oprime. Hard gate G removes objective credit but does not generally zero the constraint-fraction term; the four bespoke task graders have separately stated gate behavior.
  • Fourteen models are evaluated under restricted harness coverage, rather than a complete 14-by-7 Cartesian crossing; Grok Build is model-specific beyond the seven named common harnesses. Results must identify the model and harness.
  • Scores average three runs per task. Single-task variance and model-judge regrading/self-preference are reported; regrading by other models is not independent human validation of engineering ground truth.
  • The paper plans to release 29 of 85 tasks. This repair does not verify present release availability or independently audit codes, physics, source rights or reference optima; mean benchmark score is not deployment certification.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

PLE describes 85 tasks: 44 engineer-authored and 41 human/agent-coauthored. Coauthored tasks use expert briefs, a Claude Opus 5 Creator–Solver loop and final engineer validation. Expert tasks receive LLM-judged weighted rubric scores; most coauthored tasks combine constraint fraction with a hard-gated objective term, with four bespoke grading exceptions.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

For the pinned evaluation, Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code reports 50.6% mean task score across 85 tasks and three runs per task. This combines rubric and executable/hybrid scores and is not a strict task pass rate or the percentage of engineering assignments ready for licensed signoff.
